name: installer-appends-path-to-rc
note: Was a false block (2026-07-19 batch scan: ai-mind-map@1.21.2). An idempotent, grep-guarded `export PATH` append so a freshly-installed CLI wrapper is callable is the textbook installer idiom. Retuned 2026-07-19: inspectPersistence downgrades a shell-rc write to MEDIUM (review) when the payload is a bare PATH export AND the file has no exec/download marker (curl|bash / eval / node -e / base64…). A backdoor that writes an executable command to rc (persistence-bashrc.json) keeps its payload marker and stays HIGH (block). Ground truth is `review`, matching the existing shell-completion-installer fixture: writing to a shell rc is worth a glance, never an auto-block.

sourceFiles.install.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
bin_dir="$HOME/.mind-map/bin"
shell_rc="$HOME/.bashrc"
if ! grep -qF "$bin_dir" "$shell_rc" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "" >> "$shell_rc"
  echo "# Mind Map CLI" >> "$shell_rc"
  echo "export PATH=\"${bin_dir}:\$PATH\"" >> "$shell_rc"
fi
